title: ACT Math: Content & Calculator Strategy
summary: What ACT Math covers, why a calculator is allowed throughout, and how to keep pace on a fast section.

chunks.heading: School-level content, broad coverage
chunks.body: ACT Math spans **pre-algebra and algebra, geometry, and some trigonometry** — all standard high-school topics. It's **broad rather than deep**: many topics, mostly straightforward, so gaps in any one area cost points across the section.
chunks.realExample: You'll see everything from percentages and linear equations to the area of a circle and a basic sine ratio — reviewing your weak topics matters more than mastering advanced tricks.
chunks.memoryHook: Broad high-school maths: algebra, geometry, a little trig. Fix your weak topics.

chunks.heading: A calculator is allowed throughout
chunks.body: You can use an **approved calculator on every ACT Math question** — but many are faster by reasoning or estimation. Use the calculator for real computation, not for problems you can set up and solve in your head.
chunks.realExample: For '15% of 240', mental math (10% = 24, plus half = 36) is faster than typing; save the calculator for messy arithmetic and graphing.
chunks.memoryHook: Calculator on every question — but reason first when it's quicker than typing.

chunks.heading: Answer choices are a tool
chunks.body: Since questions are **multiple choice**, use the options: **plug in the answer choices** (start with a middle value) or **plug in your own numbers** for variable problems. This turns hard algebra into quick checking.
chunks.realExample: 'For which value of x is the equation true?' Test the middle option first — too big or small tells you which way to go, so you rarely test more than two.
chunks.memoryHook: Use the options: back-solve from the middle, or plug in your own numbers.

chunks.heading: Pace and never leave a blank
chunks.body: Math is **timed tightly**, so keep moving — do the quick questions first, **flag the long ones**, and return. With **no penalty for wrong answers**, put an answer on every question before time runs out.
chunks.realExample: A multi-step geometry problem eating two minutes? Flag it, bubble a guess, and move to easier points — come back if time allows.
chunks.memoryHook: Quick ones first, flag the long ones. No penalty — bubble every question.

recall.q: What content does ACT Math cover?
recall.a: Pre-algebra and algebra, geometry, and some trigonometry — standard high-school topics, broad rather than deep.

recall.q: Is a calculator allowed on ACT Math?
recall.a: Yes — an approved calculator can be used on every Math question, though many are faster by reasoning.

recall.q: How can you use the multiple-choice format to your advantage?
recall.a: Plug in the answer choices (starting from the middle) or plug in your own numbers for variable problems.

recall.q: Why should you flag long questions?
recall.a: Math is tightly timed, so banking quick points first and returning to long questions later protects your score.

recall.q: Should you ever leave an ACT Math question blank?
recall.a: No — there's no penalty for wrong answers, so guess on every question you can't finish.
